sense: so as to be easily seen, heard or understood

terms.gloss: plainly, clearly, so as to be understood
evidence: Cic. de Or. 1.144: deinde ut plānē et dīlūcidē
Cic. Phil. 7.17: quī plānē et Latīnē loquuntur
terms.comment: Plānē et Latīnē loquī, to speak plainly, without beating about the bush (Lewis & Short). The same word is “quite, completely” (see quite).

terms.gloss: clearly, distinctly (to the eye or the ear); aloud

evidence: Ter. And. 195: apertē vīs quae restant mē loquī
Cic. Leg. 1.36 (Lewis & Short): articulātim distīnctēque dīcere

phrases.latin: clārē oculīs videō, pernīx sum manibus, pedibus mōbilis
phrases.english: my eyes see clearly, my hands are quick, my feet are nimble

phrases.latin: in quā praecipitur prīmum, ut pūrē et Latīnē loquāmur, deinde ut plānē et dīlūcidē
phrases.english: in which the first rule is that we speak correct Latin, and the next that we speak plainly and clearly

phrases.latin: Nempe ergō apertē vīs quae restant mē loquī.
phrases.english: So you want me to say plainly what remains.

sources: Lewis & Short: planus · Lewis & Short: clarus · Lewis & Short: aperio · Lewis & Short: dilucide · Lewis & Short: distinguo
Cicero (de Or. 1.144, Phil. 7.17), Plautus (Mil. 630) and Terence (And. 195, 754) checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
